section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the passing of the righteous is even more difficult than the destruction of the Temple, and it serves to elevate the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, requiring each person in the seventh generation to emulate Avraham's work of calling out "El Olam" to reveal that the world and G-dliness are one.
section.t: And this is the matter of "the righteous one who has passed away,"
for even though there were already many concealments and obscurities and many questions and incomprehensible matters,
nevertheless, all this was not sufficient.
And in order that there be an elevation of the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He, in all worlds,
there was also the matter of the passing of the righteous,
which is difficult not only like the destruction, but even more than the destruction.
And the ultimate intention in this is that through this there will be an elevation of the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And this demands of each one of us that he know that he finds himself in the seventh generation,
that all the virtue of the seventh is that it is seventh from the first,
that the conduct of the first was that he sought nothing for himself, and not even self-sacrifice.
For he knew that his entire matter is as it is written, "And he called there in the name of Havayah, El Olam."
And analogous to the conduct of Avraham Avinu, who came to such places where they did not know of G-dliness there,
did not know of Judaism and did not know even the alef-beis, and being there, one set himself aside,
and "do not read 'vayikra' (and he called) but rather 'vayikri' (and he caused to call),"
and it is known
that in the study with the attribute of "do not read,"
both readings are valid.
And even in this, it is explicit in the Written Torah, "Vayikra."
Nevertheless, one must know that if he wants the "vayikra" to enter him,
there must be the "vayikri."
You must see that that one should not only know, but also call out.
Although until now that one knew nothing,
but now you must see that he should cry out "El Olam,"
not "El HaOlam" (the G-d of the world),
meaning that G-dliness is a matter in itself and the world is a matter in itself,
but rather that G-dliness rules and dominates over the world,
but rather that the world and G-dliness are entirely one.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that although no one can fully emulate Avraham, each person is obligated in a small measure, empowered by the leadership of the Rebbeim, and through this service the ultimate revelation will come, culminating in the connection to the very essence of Ein Sof and the final redemption led by the Rebbe.
section.t: And even though who is he and which one is he whose heart emboldens him to say,
"I will perform the service of Avraham Avinu,"
nevertheless, a small measure of it pertains to each and every one, and he is obligated in this,
and the powers for this are given to him through the conduct that the first one showed us, and from him onward until,
and including,
the conduct that was shown to us by the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe,
who paved the way and gave us powers for this.
And this itself is the preciousness of the seventh generation, that many powers were given and revealed for us.
And through service in such a manner, the essential Shechinah will be drawn down below into this physical and material world,
and it will be in an even higher level than before the sin,
and as it is stated
regarding Moshiach, "and he will be exceedingly elevated," more than Adam HaRishon, and even
as it was before the sin.
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, who bore our illnesses and suffered our pains,
and he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities,
behold, just as he saw our distress,
so too, speedily in our days and in our time, he will redeem the flock of his pasture from spiritual exile and physical exile together,
and he will stand us in a beam of light.
But all this is still only revelations,
and even more—he will connect and unite us with the essence and Atzmus of Ein Sof, blessed be He.

And this is the inner intention of the descent and chain of progression of the worlds, and the matter of sin and its rectification, and the matter of the passing of the righteous, through which there will be an elevation of the honor of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And when He takes us out of exile with a high hand,
and for all the children of Israel there will be light in their dwellings,
then Moshe and the children of Israel will sing, etc.,
"Havayah will reign forever and ever,"
(and as it is in the wording of the prayer)
and also in the language of the Targum,
"Havayah, His kingship endures forever and for all eternity."
And they conclude, "And Havayah will be King... Havayah is One and His Name is One,"
so that there will be no division between Havayah and His Name,
for all this is accomplished through the passing of the righteous,
which is more difficult even than the destruction of the Holy Temple.
And since we have already gone through all these matters,
behold, now the matter depends only on us—the seventh generation.
And we will merit to see,
with the Rebbe here below in a body and below ten handbreadths,
and he will redeem us.
